note: Jeff Orkin's GDC 2006 'Three States and a Plan: The A.I. of F.E.A.R.' paper, downloaded and read in full: GOAP mechanics (A* over world states, per-action costs, procedural preconditions/effects), replanning from failure facts, goals/actions decoupling, new enemy built late from existing actions.

Troy Humphreys, Game AI Pro ch.12 'Exploring HTN Planners through Example', downloaded and read in full: production HTN in Transformers: Fall of Cybertron, decomposition algorithm, plan-runner precondition validation, MTR replan hysteresis, HTN faster than their prior GOAP, HTN vs behavior trees.
LLM+P (Liu et al. 2023) abstract: LLM translates NL to PDDL, classical planner solves, LLM translates back; LLMs alone cannot reliably solve long-horizon planning problems.
Kambhampati et al., 'Position: LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks' (ICML 2024) abstract: LLMs as knowledge/model generators inside loops with external sound verifiers.
Guan et al. (NeurIPS 2023) abstract: GPT-4 authored PDDL models for 40+ actions; validator/human-corrected domains solved 48 challenging tasks; corrections once per domain, not per plan.
Mahdavi et al. (NeurIPS 2024) abstract: environment-feedback refinement of LLM-written PDDL; 66% average solve rate over 10 environments vs 29% for GPT-4 intrinsic chain-of-thought planning.
SayCan project page: 101 real-world tasks, 84% plan success and 74% execution success; affordance value function overrides infeasible LLM-preferred actions.
SayCan/'Do As I Can, Not As I Say' arXiv abstract: robot as the LLM's hands and eyes; grounding language via learned affordance value functions (no numbers on this page).
PlanBench (Valmeekam et al.) arXiv abstract: LLM performance on plan generation 'falls quite short' even for SOTA models (qualitative claim only; solve-rate tables are in the PDF, not this page).

Guerrilla Games article: HTN planner drives NPC high-level decisions in Decima (Killzone, Horizon Zero Dawn/Forbidden West); Prolog-like backtracking over preconditions; in-game HTN decomposition debugging.

Dana Nau's GTPyhop repository: maintained open-source HTN + goal planner with single-file core, BSD-3-Clause-Clear license, Run-Lazy-Lookahead integrated planning and acting — evidence the fixed planner is a library, not a runtime.

Excalibur.js blog (Apr 2024): working GOAP planner in TypeScript with action costs, precondition/effect chaining, Dijkstra plan selection and cancel-and-replan on world change — evidence of library-scale implementation effort in our language.

ReAct abstract (Yao et al., ICLR 2023), fetched in round 2: its +34%/+10% ALFWorld/WebShop gains are over 'imitation and reinforcement learning methods' — no classical planner or LLM+P-style solver among the baselines, so it is not counter-evidence to LLM+planner comparisons.
